title: Beyond the Biomedical Model: A Critical Review of the Approach to Chronic Pain and the Proposal of an Integrated Functional Model
authors: Alexander Muacevic; John R Adler; Luigi Pianese; Bruno Bordoni
pain_condition_detail: Chronic pain, including chronic low back pain, chronic headache, migraine, fibromyalgia, chronic fatigue syndrome, rheumatoid arthritis, irritable bowel syndrome, chronic pelvic pain.
bps_function_set: conclusion; critique or problematization; explanatory framework; intervention rationale; organizing principle; policy or practice implication
bps_operationalization_summary: The paper critiques the BPS model for neglecting nutrition, environment, and lifestyle, and proposes extending it with a 'functional dimension' focused on the extracellular matrix as biological terrain. It does not operationalize BPS through specific variables or measures but uses it as a conceptual foil for proposing a new model.
integration_mechanism_summary: No cross-domain pathways are specified. The paper asserts that biological, psychological, and social factors interact but provides no mechanistic links. The proposed functional model focuses on biological terrain and lifestyle, not on integration.
conceptual_tensions_1: The paper critiques the BPS model for neglecting nutrition and environment, yet its own proposed model adds a 'functional dimension' that is largely biological, not truly integrative
conceptual_tensions_2: The paper claims all pain is 'real' and multidimensional, but its proposed model focuses heavily on biological terrain, potentially marginalizing psychological and social factors
conceptual_tensions_3: The paper uses the BPS label extensively but does not define it beyond Engel's citation, and its critique is based on perceived gaps rather than on empirical evidence of BPS model failure
additional_observations_1: The paper is a narrative review with no systematic search strategy, no quality assessment, and no explicit inclusion criteria
additional_observations_2: The paper proposes a 'bio-psycho-functional-social model' but does not specify how the four dimensions interact mechanistically
additional_observations_3: The paper cites evidence for dietary and environmental influences on pain but does not integrate these with psychological or social mechanisms
additional_observations_4: The paper's critique of the BPS model is based on its perceived neglect of nutrition and environment, not on a systematic analysis of BPS literature
synthesis_note: This narrative review critiques the BPS model for neglecting nutrition, environment, and lifestyle, and proposes a 'bio-psycho-functional-social' model centered on the extracellular matrix. It offers no integration of the three core domains and no operationalization of BPS. Its value is as a critique and proposal, not as an empirical synthesis.
coding_rationale: Typology 'pseudo_bps' because BPS language is used but psychological and social domains are only mentioned, while biological and lifestyle domains are elaborated. Triadic integration is 'none' as no cross-domain pathways are specified. The paper is bio-dominant.

title: Beyond the Biomedical Model: A Critical Review of the Approach to Chronic Pain and the Proposal of an Integrated Functional Model
authors: Alexander Muacevic; John R Adler; Luigi Pianese; Bruno Bordoni
pain_condition_detail: Chronic pain broadly, including chronic low back pain, chronic headache/migraine, fibromyalgia, rheumatoid arthritis, chronic fatigue syndrome, and chronic pelvic pain.
context_note: Global adult population; Europe and United States prevalence and cost figures are reported.
bps_function_set: background framing; conclusion; critique or problematization; explanatory framework; intervention rationale; justification; organizing principle; policy or practice implication
bps_operationalization_summary: The review uses BPS mainly as a critique/organizing frame, then substitutes a functional model. It lists biological, psychological, nutritional, environmental, and social factors and proposes multimodal assessment/interventions, but it does not code or measure BPS variables in an empirical dataset.
integration_mechanism_summary: The proposed model posits that biological terrain, especially the extracellular matrix, inflammation, oxidative stress, mitochondrial function, nutrition, environment, lifestyle, psychological/behavioral factors, and social factors converge on peripheral and central nociceptive sensitization. Social exclusion is linked to shared brain circuits; social determinants influence incidence/prognosis. No BPS-specific mediators are measured.
conceptual_tensions_1: The paper criticizes the biomedical model for ambiguity between pain as alarm, symptom, and disease while also noting that ICD classification may medicalize pain
conceptual_tensions_2: BPS is credited with integrating biological, psychological, and social factors, but the paper argues it neglects nutrition, lifestyle, environment, and extracellular matrix mechanisms
conceptual_tensions_3: The proposed functional model is presented as more complete, yet the paper also states that research on it is still in its infancy
conceptual_tensions_4: Social factors are conceptually recognized in BPS, but the paper says they have received less empirical attention than psychological factors
conceptual_tensions_5: The paper emphasizes poor correlation between tissue damage and pain perception while also discussing structural lesions as part of biomedical explanations
additional_observations_1: This is a narrative review, not a systematic review, no formal quality or risk-of-bias assessment is reported
additional_observations_2: The paper does not empirically operationalize BPS variables through measures, coding, or pooled data
additional_observations_3: The functional dimension is treated as a fourth dimension added to biological, psychological, and social domains
additional_observations_4: Most mechanistic claims are citation-based or conceptual rather than tested within the review
synthesis_note: This review operationalizes BPS mainly as a critique of biomedicine and then replaces it with a bio-psycho-functional-social model. Biological/functional mechanisms dominate; psychological and social factors are named and linked to pain, but the paper provides more mechanistic claims for biological terrain and lifestyle/environment than for social pathways. It does not empirically operationalize BPS variables.
coding_rationale: Biological/functional content dominates and is mechanistically developed; psychosocial content is named and linked to pain. The proposed model integrates all domains through matrix/inflammation pathways, so true_integrative despite BPS being critiqued.

title: Beyond the Biomedical Model: A Critical Review of the Approach to Chronic Pain and the Proposal of an Integrated Functional Model
authors: Alexander Muacevic; John R Adler; Luigi Pianese; Bruno Bordoni
pain_condition_detail: chronic pain broadly, with focus on chronic low back pain, fibromyalgia, chronic headache, and rheumatoid arthritis
bps_function_set: background framing; critique or problematization; explanatory framework; organizing principle
bps_operationalization_summary: Organizes discussion around biomedical limitations, BPS contributions and gaps, then proposes functional model integration. BPS serves as explanatory framework but is critiqued for insufficient attention to nutrition, environment, and lifestyle. The paper does not integrate domains mechanistically but proposes a new four-dimensional model.
conceptual_tensions_1: Tension between BPS's theoretical integration and its practical failure to integrate domains mechanistically
conceptual_tensions_2: Tension between BPS's recognition of social factors conceptually versus their empirical neglect in research and practice
conceptual_tensions_3: Tension between the paper's critique of BPS as insufficient and its proposal of a new model without demonstrating its integration mechanisms
additional_observations_1: The paper positions itself as critiquing both biomedical and BPS models to justify its proposed functional model integration
additional_observations_2: The extracellular matrix is positioned as a central mediator through which nutritional, environmental, and lifestyle factors influence pain pathophysiology
additional_observations_3: The paper cites specific researchers (Totsch, Sorge, Langevin, Flor, Turk, Eisenberger, Lieberman) to support its claims rather than providing original empirical evidence
additional_observations_4: The proposed bio-psycho-functional-social model adds a 'fourth dimension' rather than truly integrating the existing three domains
synthesis_note: This narrative review critically analyzes the biomedical and bio-psycho-social models of chronic pain, arguing both are insufficiently integrated. It proposes a 'bio-psycho-functional-social' model that adds a functional dimension focused on nutrition, environment, and extracellular matrix biology. The paper does not demonstrate domain integration but critiques existing models for their lack thereof. Biological content is elaborated, psychological and social content are mentioned. The BPS label is used but the paper argues it lacks mechanistic integration between domains.
coding_rationale: BPS typology is pseudo_bps because the paper uses the label but argues it lacks integration. Domain coverage: biological elaborated (matrix, inflammation, sensitization), psychological mentioned (catastrophizing, fear, depression, anxiety), social mentioned (support, SES, access). Integration is none because domains are listed but not connected mechanistically. The paper's main contribution is critiquing BPS and proposing an alternative model.
